t:
(a) In General.—
        (1) After the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Army shall carry out the project for wastewater infrastructure, DeSoto County, Mississippi, authorized by section 219(f)(30) of Public Law 102–580, as amended, in accordance with the provisions of this subsection. 
        (2) The non-Federal interest shall be primarily responsible for carrying out work on the project referred to in paragraph (1) that is not covered by the Project Cooperation Agreement executed on May 13, 2002 or any amendments thereto, including work associated with the design, construction, 
management, and administration of the project. The non-Federal interest may carry out work on the project subject to obtaining any permits required pursuant to Federal and State laws and subject to general supervision and administrative oversight by the Secretary of the Army. 
        (3) The Federal share of project costs incurred by the non-Federal interest in carrying out work on the project as provided for in paragraph (2) shall equal 75 percent of the total cost of the work and shall be in the form of grants or reimbursements, except that the total amount of Federal funds available for the project, including that portion of the project carried out as provided for in paragraph (2), may not exceed $55,000,000.  
    (b) Technical Amendment.—Section 6006 of the Emergency Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2005 (119 Stat. 282) is amended by striking “between May 13, 2002, and September 30, 2005” and inserting “after May 13, 2002” in lieu thereof.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the non-Federal interest's role and the "Project Cooperation Agreement" show coordination with an outside party. But the section only allocates responsibility for carrying out project work, sets a 75 percent federal cost share through grants or reimbursements, and refers to a past agreement by name. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement, or right to sue before a federal decision.
fable.s: The non-Federal interest shall be primarily responsible for carrying out work on the project referred to in paragraph (1) that is not covered by the Project Cooperation Agreement executed on May 13, 2002 or any amendments thereto

opus.w: The non-Federal interest's role here is to do the project work and receive cost-sharing funds (grants or reimbursements) while the Secretary oversees it. It is not being consulted before a federal decision. The 'Project Cooperation Agreement' is a past agreement named in boilerplate, and the funding works like a grant, so neither counts as participation. Nothing in the section requires consultation, hearings, comment, advisory input or a right to sue.
opus.s: The non-Federal interest may carry out work on the project subject to obtaining any permits required pursuant to Federal and State laws and subject to general supervision and administrative oversight by the Secretary of the Army.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section refers to a "non-Federal interest" doing project work and to a "Project Cooperation Agreement," so it can look like outsiders are taking part in a federal decision. That reading fails. The agreement was signed in the past (May 13, 2002), and here the non-Federal interest only carries out construction work and receives grants or reimbursements under federal oversight. Nothing requires the Secretary to consult outside parties before a decision, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the responsibilities of a non-Federal interest in carrying out a specific infrastructure project and receiving federal funding (grants/reimbursements). The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' The non-Federal interest is performing work under federal oversight, not engaging in consultation or coordination to influence a federal policy decision. Therefore, this is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: The non-Federal interest shall be primarily responsible for carrying out work on the project referred to in paragraph (1) that is not covered by the Project Cooperation Agreement executed on May 13, 2002 or any amendments thereto, including work associated with the design, construction, management, and administration of the project.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "non-Federal interest" (a local government or entity) is participating in the decision-making because they are responsible for carrying out the work and obtaining permits. However, this is essentially an application for a grant or a contract to perform work, which the definition explicitly excludes ("It does not include applications for benefits or grants"). The non-Federal interest is executing a project under federal oversight, not consulting with the federal government on a policy decision or rulemaking. The interaction is administrative and financial, not participatory in the sense of influencing a federal decision through consultation, hearings, or advisory roles.
